# 🐭 Mouse: Admiral Cloudbeard

| Admiral Cloudbeard |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: Floating Islanders (Sky Pirate) |  |  |  |

| Behold the "Sultan of the Skies", the "Conqueror of the Clouds", the "Tyrant at Ten Thousand Feet": Admiral Cloudbeard, leader of the Sky Pirates! This malevolent marauder is undefeated in hand-to-hook combat thanks to his massive, untamed beard making him an impossible target. His opponents can never tell where the beard ends and the Admiral begins. It's so thick that swords get stuck in it and shots get completely absorbed. Legend has it that his mighty beard has even survived being shot with a cannonball!<br>There is only one sky dweller brave enough to face the Admiral head-on and capable enough to come out of it alive and intact, his arch-nemesis: Ronza! The Admiral and his legion of ne'er-do-wells have been hunting Ronza and her enormous cache of chrome treasures for as long as they've sailed the skies. Unfortunately for them, she has consistently managed to elude, confuse, defeat, and humiliate Cloudbeard and his cronies at every turn. The Admiral has vowed to never give up on his quest for vengeance against that legendary sky captain, no matter how many limbs it costs him.<br>♫ We pirate, pillage, and plight,<br>Attacking every ship in flight!<br>Those that oppose, face the beard that he grows,<br>And he'll never give up the fight! ♫<br>- An ancient sky shanty |  |  |  |

The Barnacle Beautician Mouse is a breed of mouse found in the Sunken City. It is known to drop Barnacles and Sand Dollars as loot.

| Scouring the deep for the most beautiful of Barnacles, this beautician loves the look and feel of freshly-formed Barnacle shells, moulding and shaping them into fine jewelry and accessories. Always on the lookout, her eyes just light up whenever she spots a particularly pretty bunch or a new candidate to become part of her latest fashions. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 575 |  |  |

## Cheese Preference

The Barnacle Beautician Mouse has no specific preference for any kind of cheese.

## Hunting Strategy

The Barnacle Beautician Mouse is susceptible only to Hydro weapons. It can be found in the Rocky Outcrop and Shipwreck zones while on a Dive in the Sunken City.

## Event Participation

### Spring Egg Hunt

- The Barnacle Beautician Mouse drops the Barnacle Egg during the annual Spring Egg Hunt.

# 🐭 Mouse: Battering Ram Mouse

> **Type**: Mouse | **Category**: Mice | **Source**: [Battering Ram Mouse](https://mhwiki.hitgrab.com/wiki/index.php/Battering_Ram_Mouse)

The Battering Ram is a breed of mouse found in Fort Rox. They are not known to drop any loot.

| Battering Ram Mouse |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: Meteorite Miners (Special) |  |  |  |
| Mouse Statistics |  |  |  |
| Points: | 900 | Gold: | 100 |
| Location & Attraction Info |  |  |  |
| Required Power Types: | ArcaneShadow | Other Requirements: | Any Night Phase |
| Cheese: | Standard Cheese | Charm: | None |
| Locations: | Fort Rox | Loot: | None |
| Links |  |  |  |
| Larry's Loot Lexicon: | MouseHunt Info Page | Image: | Image Link |
| Well-dressed and with a wide grin, this cowboy has a gleam of meteorite shining in his eyes and he won't stop until he gets more! Wielding a solid column of meteorite rock, you better catch him before he catches your walls!<br>When attacking your wall with his battering ram, it produces so much force that it explodes into a cloud of miniscule fragments and dust.<br>He will cause damage to your fort wall even if caught, so avoid him at all costs!<br>Rumor has it that this mouse was specially trained in the light of the moon, which gives him his frenzied strength. However, he ironically hates the taste and sight of Crescent and Moon Cheese, recoiling from the imitation moonlight and running off to protect his precious columns of rock! |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 830 |  |  |

## Preferred Cheese

The Battering Ram Mouse prefers Standard Cheeses, and will avoid traps baited with Crescent or Moon Cheese.

## Hunting Strategy

Arcane and Shadow traps are less effective against the Battering Ram Mouse. Other Power Types are ineffective.
The Battering Ram Mouse can be encountered during the Twilight, Midnight, Pitch, Utter Darkness, and First Light phases at Nighttime and at Dawn while hunting with Standard Cheeses in Fort Rox. The Battering Ram is extremely difficult to catch; one strategy is to wait until the Power Enchantment upgrade has been completed, then hunt with Tower Mana activated so as to have a chance at an instant defeat. The Moonbeam Barrier Trap has a 100% catch rate for this mouse.

The Betta Mouse has no specific preference for any kind of cheese.

## Preferred Cheese

Caravan Guard mice have no specific preference for any kind of cheese. In fact, they are known to have an aversion to SUPER|brie+ cheese and are known to avoid traps baited with them.

## Hunting Strategy

None of the weapon types are very effective or effective against Caravan Guard mice. Physical, Hydro, and Tactical traps are less effective, and the rest are ineffective.

When a hunter fails to capture a Caravan Guard Mouse, one of the following messages will appear on the Hunter's Journal:

Or

When failing to catch a Caravan Guard Mouse, additional mice will be added to the current wave. If a hunter has friends currently in the Sandtail Desert region, there is a chance that additional mice will not be added. A minimum of one friend is needed in helping to prevent reinforcements from arriving. However, no matter how many friends a hunter has in this region, it is not a 100% guarantee that reinforcements will be prevented.

Since failure to catch a Caravan Guard mouse carries a risk of increasing the number of mice remaining to be defeated, hunters wishing to avoid this risk are advised to use SUPER|brie+ cheese to minimize the possibility of encountering this mouse. Additionally, fewer Caravan Guard mice are attracted when any Warpath charm is armed (Warpath Archer, Warpath Soldier, Warpath Scout, Warpath Cavalry, Warpath Mage, or the super variants of these charms). In particular, arming a Warpath Mage Charm or Warpath Cavalry Charm in Wave 1 can be an effective way to adjust the population without having any charms consumed.

After capturing the Carmine the Apothecary in the Living Garden, the hunter is transferred to a different version of the location, the Twisted Garden. This illness spread like wildfire and it seemed nothing could be done, until finally Carmine arrived with faintly-glowing poultices and potions and miraculously cured everyone in a single day.<br>Since then, she's been the town's famed and well-loved apothecary, able to cure diseases that don't even have names yet. Sneaking into the Living Garden has allowed her to gather the Garden Essences necessary to accomplish this task, but something sinister happened to her there, and she's become more than just an apothecary - for reasons unknown she's raised an army of mice that attack anyone entering the Garden, and is able to wield incredible powers and seemingly span worlds with her magic!<br>The question is, how did a simple apothecary gain the ability to control world-rending magic, and what does this mean for Gnawnia as a whole? |  |  |  |

# 🐭 Mouse: Chess Master

> **Type**: Mouse | **Category**: Mice | **Source**: [Chess Master](https://mhwiki.hitgrab.com/wiki/index.php/Chess_Master)

The Chess Master is a breed of mouse found in the Zugzwang's Tower. They are known to drop Ancient Relic, Master Bindings and occasionally, Zugzwang's Left Sock, as loot. Hunters are transported to the Seasonal Garden upon catching the Chess Master.

| Chess Master |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: Wizard's Pieces (Misc) |  |  |  |
| Mouse Statistics |  |  |  |
| Points: | 119,600 | Gold: | 19,000 |
| Location & Attraction Info |  |  |  |
| Required Power Types: | Tactical | Other Requirements: | None |
| Cheese: | Checkmate | Charm: | None |
| Locations: | Zugzwang's Tower | Loot: | Ancient RelicMaster BindingsZugzwang's Left Sock |
| Links |  |  |  |
| Larry's Loot Lexicon: | MouseHunt Info Page | Image: | Image Link |
| Atop the tall tower, in the midst of an isle of madness, sits the maddest mouse of them all: the Chess Master. The Seasonal Garden and the Tower answer to his whims, changing with his mercurial moods. Behind his glowing white eyes lies the mind which produced the rage of the Technic King, and the cold brutality of the Mystic Queen. The Chess Master has the potential to create anything- but he is more likely to destroy everything. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 278 |  |  |

## Preferred Cheese

The Chess Master is only attracted to Checkmate Cheese.

## Hunting Strategy

The Chess Master can be attracted using Checkmate Cheese once the Hunter catches either a Mystic King or a Technic King and stays in the tower (by either using Checkmate Cheese or Stalemate Charm).

Tactical traps are very effective against the Chess Master, while all others are ineffective.

Catching the Chess Master will cause the Hunter to be moved to the Seasonal Garden unless Stalemate Charm is also armed. If the Hunter manages to stay in Zugzwang's Tower after catching the Chess Master (by using Stalemate Charm), they can attempt to catch more mice, including the Chess Master itself.

Catching a Chess Master with a Uncharged Scholar Charm armed will add a Scholar Charm to the Hunter's inventory. This charm can be used to attract Zurreal the Eternal in Crystal Library.

## Preferred Cheese

Crimson Commander mice have been found to be especially attracted to SUPER|brie+ cheese.

## Special Effect

Upon capturing a Crimson Commander Mouse, the following message will be displayed on the Hunter's Journal:
By capturing a Crimson Commander Mouse I demoralized the remaining mice in this wave!
My current streak was x.
x of each mouse have retreated!

## Hunting Strategy

Catching a Crimson Commander Mouse, particularly during a streak of unbroken catches of a specific Marching Flame class or unit (Archer, Scout, Warrior, Cavalry, Mage or Artillery), will help to reduce the remaining quantities of mice that require defeating in that current Wave.
Hunters have the option of arming Warpath Commander's Charms or Super Warpath Commander's Charms to help increase the likelihood of encountering a Crimson Commander Mouse.

During Wave One, Crimson Commander Mice retreat when there are less than 11 mice remaining in the troops to be defeated.
During Wave Two, Crimson Commander Mice retreat when there are less than 19 mice remaining in the troops to be defeated.
During Wave Three, Crimson Commander Mice retreat when there are less than 27 mice remaining in the troops to be defeated.

## Event Participation

- The Crimson Commander Mouse drops the Warpath Egg during the annual Spring Egg Hunt.

| This mouse may be the most difficult to catch in the Lost City. Not only is she powerful and hidden by a curse, but she is also the mouse that supplies this small settlement with Garden Essences smuggled straight from the Living Garden. No one knows how a mouse partially trapped in another dimension can even travel to the Garden but this mouse is proof that she has found a way. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 419 |  |  |

## Preferred Cheese

Essence Collector mice have been found to be only attracted to Dewthief Camembert.

## Hunting Strategy

Essence Collector is a member of the Lost City mouse group. As such all power types except Arcane weapons are ineffective against it.

It can only be attracted during the Lost Curse Minigame.

# 🐭 Mouse: Force Fighter

> **Type**: Mouse | **Category**: Mice | **Source**: [Force Fighter](https://mhwiki.hitgrab.com/wiki/index.php/Force_Fighter)

During MouseHunt's Fifth Birthday, five new mice decided to form an attack force against Ronza's airship. Known as the Force Fighter Five, each of these mice had their own colored costume, and each dropped loot of multiple Force Fighter Action Figures matching their color. Additionally, the mice could join forces into a larger Super FighterBot MegaSupreme robot, terrorizing the event.

Thankfully, the mice were careless, and also dropped Robot Scraps as loot. A hunter could collect 10 of each color of scrap, as well as buy a Repurposed Robot Head from Ronza, in order to create the Ultra MegaMouser MechaBot Trap. This weapon was the only way to beat the combined Force Fighters, and earn the Crushed Birthday Cake Base as a reward for saving the birthday celebrations.

| Mouse | Collectible | Scrap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Force Fighter Blue | Force Fighter Blue Action Figure | Blue Leg Robot Scrap |
| Force Fighter Green | Force Fighter Green Action Figure | Green Arm Robot Scrap |
| Force Fighter Pink | Force Fighter Pink Action Figure | Pink Leg Robot Scrap |
| Force Fighter Red | Force Fighter Red Action Figure | Red Chest Robot Scrap |
| Force Fighter Yellow | Force Fighter Yellow Action Figure | Yellow Arm Robot Scrap |

Progress in building the new weapon could be tracked in the Heads-up Display at Ronza's Traveling Shoppe. Upon catching the tenth mouse of any color, this additional message appeared in the Hunter's Journal:

After collecting all 50 scraps, another message appeared in the Hunter's Journal:

After a hunter has all 50 scraps and the Repurposed Robot Head, the Heads-up Display adds a message "You've got the parts! Complete the trap in Ronza's Shoppe!"

After buying the Ultra MegaMouser MechaBot Trap, the Heads-Up Display changes to a picture of the two robots facing one another, initially with a message "Arm your Ultra MegaMouser MechaBot Trap to fight back!". There is also a Boss meter at the bottom of the Heads-up Display, with a hint that states "Each Super FighterBot MegaSupreme catch does 10 damage to their HP! The Super FighterBot MegaSupreme has 100/100 HP."

After arming the Ultra MegaMouser MechaBot Trap, the original five Force Fighter mice cannot be attracted, but it is then possible to attract the Super FighterBot MegaSupreme mouse. Each failed hunt that attracted the Super FighterBot MegaSupreme shows an animation of it firing a barrage of missiles at the hunter; and each successful catch shows an animation of the hunter's MegaMouser charging the FighterBot with a large explosion. Each catch weakens the FighterBot by 10 HP, with the following message in the Hunter's Journal:

Finally, after defeating the FighterBot 10 times, the hunter was awarded the Crushed Birthday Cake Base, along with this message in the journal:

Thereafter, a third Heads-up Display background is shown, with a View again link for replaying the final battle.

### Force Fighter Action Figure

All five action figure collectibles (blue, green, pink, red, and yellow) have the same description. There was no limit on the amount a hunter could collect. The Event Scoreboard allowed hunters to compare who had collected the most.

During the annual MouseHunt Birthday, Hunters were able to trade in these collectibles for Party Charms at the event Charm Shoppe, but have been rendered obsolete since the conclusion of Birthday Party Zone, Mousehunt's Ninth Birthday

### Robot Scrap

All five scrap types (blue leg, green arm, pink leg, red chest, and yellow arm) have the same description. A hunter could own at most 10 of a given color scrap at the same time.

### Repurposed Robot Head

This head could be purchased from Ronza's Traveling Shoppe General Store for 100,000 gold, and could be returned for the same value. A hunter could own at most one at a time.

As the Moussu Picchu Inhabitants below battle endlessly for dominance of the weather, the resulting stalemate allows the queen to slumber for generations.<br>Once, long ago, she would appear high above the land anywhere a lightning cloud hovered, visiting the many realms of mice across Gnawnia, her tail smacking the ground like lightning as she plucked treasures with it to add to her hoard. Slowly but surely, disturbed by the intensifying battle in the lands below and the low rumble of impending thunderstorms in the clouds upon which she rests, she begins to rouse from her deep sleep...<br>Soon, and without warning, Ful'Mina, the Mountain Queen, will descend upon the lands with great fury to bring order to the chaos through the destructive force of her indomitable lightning storms. |  |  |  |

Like all mice in the Gnawnia Rift, Goliath Field mice can be caught with any power type except Parental. However, due to all types except Rift being less effective against the mice in the area, it is in a hunter's best interest to focus on catching one Goliath Field as soon as possible, to gain the Crystal Tower trap (and the Riftwalker Set bonus if the hunter already has the Rift Base), to make all mice in the area easier to catch. If a hunter does not want to use an Ultimate charm, then Ultimate Power Charms coupled with the hunter's strongest non-Rift trap show a remarkable improvement in catch rate compared to any other charm.

Catching a hunter's first Goliath Field Mouse leaves a message in the Hunter's Journal:

Since the detention dungeon is the last place that any student would want to find themselves, there is only one mouse that you will ever find roaming the halls at this school and that's the Hall Monitor.<br>Armed with the latest edition of the rules compendium and their signature silver mouse whistle, this strict scholarly sentinel stalks tirelessly up and down the halls with their trusty sidekick, Deborah the Safety Dragon, in search of any student bold or foolish enough to be cutting class.<br>Any hunter who finds themselves wandering the halls of the School of Sorcery is advised to enroll in a class as soon as possible or else they will suffer the shrill sound of the silver whistle, Deborah's foamy, disapproving growl, and worst of all, the Hall Monitor's most powerful and infamous spell: the Recitation of Infinite Rules! |  |  |  |

# 🐭 Mouse: Hardboiled Mouse

> **Type**: Mouse | **Category**: Mice | **Source**: [Hardboiled Mouse](https://mhwiki.hitgrab.com/wiki/index.php/Hardboiled_Mouse)

The Hardboiled Mouse is an Event Mouse found during the annual Spring Egg Hunt event.

| Hardboiled Mouse |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: Event Mice (Spring Egg Hunt) |  |  |  |
| Mouse Statistics |  |  |  |
| Points: | 3,200 | Gold: | 125 |

| Required Power Types: | All types | Other Requirements: | See current Spring Egg Hunt location |

| Rain.<br>It never seemed to be sunny-side up in Gnawnia. At least, not whenever I was working a case. This one was a doozie but I knew I was close to cracking it.<br>Like everything else in this crazy world, it all came down to a doe. Easy enough on the eyes, I suppose, but when you're talking about eyes, you have to be careful. This doe had crazy eyes, and a crazy plan hatching behind them.<br>Situations like this never go over-easy. See, she'd gotten ahold of the last free Golden Egg in Gnawnia, and wired up this crazy contraption to it.<br>"A scrambler, get it?" she asked, eyes rolling. And then she laughed. That laugh. Like loose nails rattling around in a jar. Or on reflection, loose screws.<br>Her plan as I figured it, was to scramble up all the Eggscavators in the land and throw mice and hunters alike into wild confusion. Her motivation, however, was about as clear as runny yolk.<br>I had tracked her through Gnawnia's back alleys, from Cheese Bars to Mad Scientist Surplus Shoppes, and finally cornered her here. Still, she didn't seem upset. More pleased, actually. Perhaps at the opportunity to show off.<br>"I'm going to Scramble everything, do you understand? Everything! Ah ha ha ha ha!" That laugh again.<br>"Look, sister," I said, stepping carefully closer. "I know you think you have a job to do, but I do too. I'm here to bring you in, and you can come peacefully with me, or well, I know there's a few hunters around looking for you too, and you're gonna get poached if you're not careful."<br>At the mention of hunters, she flinched visibly. Her shell was crumbling, but breaking her so close to the frying pan was risky. I decided to take it easier on her. "If you hand over the device and come along quietly, we can put you in the Hunter Protection Program. You'll get a new name, a new house, a new job..."<br>"No!" she cried. "No new job! Science, mad science forever!" Then she pulled another strange-looking device from inside her tinfoil jacket, thumbed a button on top, and threw it at me. I ducked, there was a bright flash, and when I looked again, she was gone.<br>As my vision recovered, I noticed a trail of oil, nuts, and bolts leading away. My keen detective sense told me she'd gone that way, so I decided to follow.<br>She couldn't escape me for long. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 465 |  |  |

## Hunting Strategy

To attract the Heart of the Meteor, the Hunter has to arm Sunrise Cheese in Heart of the Meteor phase in Fort Rox. A Fort Rox Portal Projector is required to enter this phase. Doing so will consume the Projector and add a Ruined Portal Projector to the Hunter's inventory.

The Heart of the Meteor is primarily weak to Arcane traps, though Shadow traps can be used to lesser effect.
The Hunter's Fort defenses have no effect in this phase. Tower Mana cannot be armed while hunting in this phase.
The Heart of the Meteor's power will be lowered with each attraction, to the point where it is a guaranteed catch on the 10th attraction.

Catching the Heart of the Meteor will return the Hunter to the Dawn phase and disarms Sunrise Cheese.

Upon catching the Heart of the Meteor, the following message is displayed in the Hunter's Journal:

The Hunter may enter the Heart of the Meteor phase multiple times without affecting their Wall health or progress in the Dawn phase.

# 🐭 Mouse: King Grub Mouse

The King Grub Mouse is a breed of mouse that can be found in the Sand Crypts, and is known to drop Dol Essences, Est Essences, Fel Essences and Lunaria Petals as loot.

| King Grub Mouse |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: Sand Dunes Mice |  |  |  |
| Mouse Statistics |  |  |  |
| Points: | 35,000 | Gold: | 8,500 |
| Location & Attraction Info |  |  |  |
| Required Power Types: | Shadow | Other Requirements: | See Salting Minigame |

| This oversized grub has refused to morph into its true form. Instead, it continues to consume and increase its mass to an alarming size. This self-declared King rules through fear in the Sand Crypt, commanding other mice to bring him food and defend his lair at all costs. Luckily for him, the mice fear him more than they do a hunter's trap - plus it's not too hard to swipe the cheese without the King Grub mouse knowing.<br>Being a gigantic grub is about the equivalent to being a gigantic baby - not too smart but prone to loud and sometimes dangerous tantrums. Mice steer clear of him as best as they can, which is okay because he prefers it that way.<br>The short of all this, is that you'll never attract the King Grub to your trap without liberally slathering it with an appealing scent to attract him, and you'll never defeat him without heavily salting your trap for an added boost. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 428 |  |  |

## Hunting Strategy

Normally, King Grub Mouse can only be attracted with Graveblossom Camembert and Grub Scent Charm armed.
It can also be attracted without Grub Scent Charm if Smelly Sodium Base is armed and salt level is at 50.

King Grub Mouse is a member of the Sand Dunes Mice group. As such all power types except Shadow are ineffective against it.

Salting is recommended before trying to catch King Grub Mouse.

| Guarding all of the inmates of the dungeon is a difficult and tiring task and as this slothful sentry is well aware, the easiest way to deal with a difficult task is... not to do it! ## Cheese Preference

Lethargic Guard Mouse is only attracted to Beanster Cheese.

The Lethargic Guard Mouse can only be attracted after planting a Short Vine to the Dungeon Floor.

Physical power type is effective against Lethargic Guard Mouse.
All other types are ineffective.

Lethargic Guard Mouse can drop:

- Lavish Lapis Bean

## Preferred Cheese

## Hunting Strategy

Arcane traps are very effective against the Monster of the Meteor. Shadow traps are of normal effectiveness.
Monster of the Meteor mice can only be encountered during the dawn phase in Fort Rox.

Upon catching the Monster of the Meteor, the following message is displayed in the Hunter's Journal:
Capturing the Monster of the Meteor enraged him and his company of guards.
From now on, any mouse I fail to capture will do x00% damage to my fort wall!

With every catch the % damage will increase with an additional 100%, and the HUD will display a different level of irritation with each catch:

### Wall Damage

When Hunters reach the Dawn phase, each catch of a Monster of the Meteor will multiply the damage effects to the wall by an additional 100%. Any FTC of a Monster of the Meteor or Dawn Guardian will result in greater damage to the Hunter's wall. Damage from encountering a Battering Ram Mouse is not multiplied.

| Catch | Anger Level | Damage Multiplier | FTC Damage | Red Box FTC Damage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Irritated | 100% | 3 | 5 |

## Preferred Cheese

Monstrous Black Widow mice have been found to be especially attracted to Lactrodectus Lancashire, to the point that any other kind of cheese will simply not suffice.

## Loot

The loot dropped by Monstrous Black Widow depends on the number of factions that are at 50 rage. Generally, she drops better loot as more factions are at 50 rage. With at least one faction, Rift Ultimate Power Charm is added to the loot; with two factions, Rift Ultimate Luck Charm is added to the mix, and with all three factions, Plankrun's Whisker Woods Rift Notes (if not already possessed) and another random item are added as loot.

| Factions at 50 rage | Loot (cumulative) |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Ancient Relic<br>Divine Orb<br>Rift Cherries<br>Rift-torn Roots<br>Sap-filled Thorns<br>Widow's Web (Chance of +1 Web added at 3 Factions at 50 rage) |
| 1 | Rift Ultimate Power Charm |
| 2 | Rift Ultimate Luck Charm |
| 3 | Bolt of Cloth<br>Calcified Rift Mist<br>Cherry Charm<br>Gnarled Charm<br>Gnarled Potion<br>Greater Wicked Gnarly Potion<br>Luck Charm<br>Lucky Power Charm<br>Magical String Cheese<br>Plankrun's Whisker Woods Rift Notes<br>Power Charm<br>Radioactive Sludge<br>Rift Power Charm<br>Rope<br>Satchel of Gold (10,000, 50,000 or 100,000 gold)<br>Scrap Metal<br>Splintered Wood<br>Stagnant Charm<br>Super Luck Charm<br>Super Power Charm<br>Super Rotten Charm<br>Taunting Charm<br>Wicked Gnarly Potion |

## Hunting Strategy

Monstrous Black Widow mice are weak to Rift Traps, and is the first Rift Walker mouse that is not susceptible to any other weapon power type. They can only be attracted by Lactrodectus Lancashire, which is only effective when all three factions have a Rage of at least 25. The probability of attracting Monstrous Black Widow instead of any other mouse goes up as a hunter has more rage.

A hunter will generally need to use some funnel charms (Cherry, Gnarled, or Stagnant) to reach the required rage, since without them, the usual mouse population generally favors the first faction to reach 25 to reach that mini-boss before the other two factions have a chance to reach 25. Therefore, one strategy for getting all three factions to 50 rage is to start a cycle with normal hunting reaches 25 rage for one faction, then use funnel charms to get the other two factions to 25 (the chance of a +2 rage mouse from the first faction will make the other two factions reach 25 faster), then resume normal hunting to get one faction to 48 or 49, then resume funnel hunting until all factions are at 48 or 49. As long as no faction is at 50, then there is no risk of a mini-boss resetting rage and losing out on the chance for a Monstrous Black Widow. But as soon as a faction is at 50, the hunter has to switch to a strategy that reduces the risk of resetting rage by an accidental mini-boss catch, either by arming a Taunting Charm, or intentionally switching to a much weaker trap setup that can still catch the remaining regular mice needed while missing the mini-boss.

Overall, the safest way to catch a Monstrous Black Widow without risking an accidental mini-boss catch is to reach the highest rage possible without hitting 50. Since funnel charms attract mice that can increase the rage by 6, any hunt with a funnel charm when the rage is 44 or over risks hitting 50. Therefore, funnel charms should only be used as long as the rage is 43 or below. When all three factions are over 43, the Monstrous Black Widow is at its highest attraction rate without risking hitting 50 rage on any faction.

## Event Participation

### Spring Egg Hunt

- The Monstrous Black Widow Mouse drops the Enlarged Rift Egg and the Rift Venom Egg during the annual Spring Egg Hunt.

# 🐭 Mouse: Mouse Group

> **Type**: Mouse | **Category**: Mice | **Source**: [Mouse Group](https://mhwiki.hitgrab.com/wiki/index.php/Mouse_Group)

Mouse Groups are groups of mice which have similar weaknesses or exist in similar locations. No mouse is currently in more than one mouse group, even if that mouse exists in many locations. The mice of each group are listed roughly in order of weakest to strongest.

Please see the Effectiveness page for detailed information on which mice are weak to which trap Power Types, as not all mice in the same group have the exact same weaknesses.

## Mouse Groups

### Indigenous Mice

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane, Forgotten, Hydro, Draconic, Law, Rift

Indigenous mice live in the core hunting areas, such as Gnawnia, The Harbor and The Mountain. Physical traps work best against indigenous mice, and they prefer normal flavours of cheese, such as cheddar, marble, swiss, brie or SUPER|brie+.

A list of Indigenous Mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups:

| Misc.<br>Shiny Seekers<br>Great Gnawnian Games; and<br>Rare Rodent |
| --- |

### Dock Dwellers

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane, Forgotten, Hydro, Draconic, Law

Blimey! These pirates are frequently found harassing ships at the Harbour in search of valuable cargo to steal.

A list of Dock Dwellers can be found here.

### Mountain Mice

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane, Forgotten, Hydro, Draconic, Law

Although these mice originate from the mountain range in Gnawnia, a few of these breeds can occasionally be found in other locations.

A list of Mountain Mice can be found here.

### Forest Guild

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane, Forgotten, Hydro, Draconic, Law

Members of the Forest Guild dwell in Whisker Woods, and their traits reflect their green surroundings. Physical and tactical weapons work quite well on members of the Guild, but normal bait may not always work. While weaker Forest Guild members enjoy normal cheese, the powerful Silth mouse will only respond to something. . . extremely gnarly.

A list of Forest Guild mice can be found here.

### Lab Experiments

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane, Forgotten, Hydro, Law

The various radioactive materials at the Laboratory have mutated some of these mice into powerful adversaries! Pay special care when hunting the fearsome Monster Mouse!

A list of Lab Experiments mice can be found here.

### The Shadow Clan

Known Weaknesses: Shadow, Arcane, Forgotten

These spoo-oo-ky mice like to shamble around graveyards and catacombs, looking for their favorite snack, Radioactive Blue Cheese. If you've come to the graveyard in search of the infamous Lycan Mouse, however, Moon Cheese might just make it howl.

A list of The Shadow Clan mice can be found here.

### Digby Dirt Dwellers

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane

The Digby Dirt Dwellers all share a love of subterranean life, whether they're building tunnels, hanging out in the sediment, or just picking up shiny stones they find on the ground. They are weak against physical traps, and are only attracted to the subtle vibration of Limelight Cheese.

A list of Digby Dirt Dwellers can be found here.

### Followers of Furoma

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Tactical

These martial mice are weak to tactical traps. Most of them are attracted to normal cheese, but if Hunters want to navigate the Dojo, there are some things they should remember. Students will leave their training for Maki cheese any day, but Masters are only attracted to specific cheese made from the tokens dropped by students. As for the Master of the Dojo, Hunters should try hard to make his stomach rumble. Still looking for a challenge after defeating the Master? Bait your trap with the rare Onyx Gorgonzola, and you might meet the Sensei himself.

A list of Followers of Furoma can be found here.

### The Forgotten Mice

Known Weaknesses: Shadow, Arcane, Forgotten

Forgotten Mice have served the will of the Acolyte Mouse for untold centuries, working to release him from his prison in the Acolyte Realm. Forgotten minions prefer Radioactive Blue or Ancient Cheese, but the overlords of the Acolyte Realm are only attracted to Runic Cheese.

A list of The Forgotten Mice can be found here.

### Aquatic Order

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Tactical, Hydro

The Aquatic Order inhabits the vast blue seas of Rodentia, and a few other related waterways around Gnawnia. Normal cheese will suffice to tempt them out of the deeps, but make sure to equip a Hydro trap, or the Aquatic mouse you're after may well end up being the one that got away.

A list of Aquatic Order mice can be found here.

### The Elub Tribe

Known Weaknesses: Hydro

Notable for their blue garments and love of the seashore, the Elub Tribe can only be caught using Hydro traps. Normal cheese does not interest them, so keep plenty of Gouda or SUPER|brie+ on hand. The village elders are quite elusive, but rumor has it that Shell Cheese can bring them out of hiding.

A list of The Elub Tribe mice can be found here.

### The Nerg Tribe

Known Weaknesses: Tactical

The Nerg tribe are masters of disguise, and only a tactical trap can penetrate their defenses. The younger tribe members prefer Gouda or SUPER|brie+, but the elders will only pit themselves against your trap if a piece of Gumbo cheese is on the line.

A list of The Nerg Tribe mice can be found here.

### The Derr Tribe

Known Weaknesses: Physical

The Derr Tribe have managed to survive for centuries in a harsh desert, growing stronger to combat the dry wind and the heat. As a result, only Physical traps can hold them. The tribes-mice of Derr enjoy Gouda or SUPER|brie+, but Crunchy cheese is required to draw the attention of the tribal elders.

A list of The Derr Tribe mice can be found here.

### The Dreaded Horde

Known Weaknesses: Shadow

These monstrous mice live deep in the Jungle of dread. Horde members respond only to Havarti, and each mouse prefers a different spice mixed in with their cheese. The Horde may be a picky bunch, but catching them is well worth the effort, for they are the guardians of the parts to an ancient trap capable of catching mice older than Gnawnia itself!

A list of The Dreaded Horde mice can be found here.

### Draconic Brood

Known Weaknesses: Draconic

From the depths of the volcanic rock around Dracano spring the Draconic Brood, a rare and dangerous group of mice who share a love for fire and destruction. A Draconic type trap, equipped with insanely spicy Inferno Havarti Cheese, has the best chance of ending a Draconic mouse's rampage.

A list of Draconic Brood mice can be found here.

### Balack's Banished

Known Weaknesses: Shadow, Arcane, Forgotten

These accursed mice have been twisted by the dark enchantment surrounding Balack's Cove. The sweet smell of Vanilla Stilton will draw them in from beyond the grave, but if you seek the Lich Elders, or Balack himself, Vengeful Vanilla Stilton will give your trap extra bite. The Banished can be caught using Shadow, Arcane, or Forgotten traps, but Forgotten traps work best against Balack and his Elder minions.

A list of Balack's Banished mice can be found here.

### Gauntlet Gladiators

Known Weaknesses: none officially listed

The legion of mice swarming the King's Gauntlet comes from diverse and untold regions, and therefore their individual taste in cheese, and their power type differs as greatly as their lands of origin. Hunters seeking to take their trapping skills to the next level should look for special potion drops from the mice they are currently hunting. Only then will they possess the proper bait (and the proper knowledge of power types) to reach the top.

A list of Gauntlet Gladiators mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups, called Tiers:

| Tier 1: Puppet<br>Tier 2: Thief<br>Tier 3: Melee<br>Tier 4: Bard | Tier 5: Magic<br>Tier 6: Noble<br>Tier 7: Dust<br>Tier 8: The Eclipse |
| --- | --- |

### Seasonal Soldiers

Known Weaknesses: Tactical

From the ever-changing vistas of Zugzwang's garden come the Seasonal Soldiers, a group of mice who have been infused with the magic of the four seasons. If you want to draw these 'seasoned' veterans in, use normal cheeses, such as swiss, brie, gouda or SUPER|brie+ and a tactical trap, but know this: The Hunter seeking true mastery of the Seasonal Soldiers must find the special weaknesses that are unique to each season.

A list of Seasonal Soldiers can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the season the Seasonal Garden is in:

| Winter<br>Spring<br>Summer; and<br>Fall |
| --- |

### Wizard's Pieces

Known Weaknesses: Tactical

Fighting a perpetual battle within the enchanted halls of Zugzwang's tower are the Wizard's Pieces, warrior mice who follow a complicated and rigid set of rules in order to achieve victory. On one side is the Technic army, brimming with metalworks and gadgets, and on the other, the Mystic army, who use spells and charms to gain the upper hand. You'll have to defeat the entire chess set to reach the king, so plan your moves carefully!

A list of Wizard's Pieces mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups:

| Misc<br>Mystic; and<br>Technic |
| --- |

### Zurreal's Breed

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Tactical

This group of mice have specifically adapted to infiltrate Zugzwang's Library. Their non-organic mix of magic and technology allow them to pass safely through the library's specialized security where they are keen to tear the almost infinite amount of research to shreds.

A list of Zurreal's Breed mice can be found here.

### Icewing's Invasion

Known Weaknesses: Hydro

Swarming down from the icy north, these mice are pounding on the very walls of Gnawnia's castle! While they're all repulsed by Hydro weapons (who likes being wet when it's cold?), they seems to have a particular weakness to hot Hydro weapons. Arm yourself accordingly and head out, hunters!

A list of Icewing's Invasion mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups, based on how deep the Hunter travels through the Iceberg:

| Misc.<br>Bergling<br>Tunnel Rat<br>Brute | Bomb Squad<br>Zealot; and<br>Icewing's Generals<br>*nocontent |
| --- | --- |

### Wild Bunch

Known Weaknesses: Law

Hardy and untamed, these varmints of the Claw Shot City have adapted to the harsh conditions of the wild frontier. It takes strong will and independence to survive far from the cozy confines of city life, and these mice have grown accustomed to the freedom from the Law.

A list of Wild Bunch mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups:

| Misc.<br>Crew; and<br>Ringleader |
| --- |

### Train Robbers

Known Weaknesses: Law

These mice have one thing on their minds: Raid the supplies on the Gnawnian Express or prevent it from completing its trip. Nothing else matters to these lawless mice and they will fight to sabotage the train at all costs!

A list of Train Robbers mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups, based on the different phases of the train ride:

| Passenger<br>Depot Worker<br>Automice<br>Raider; and<br>Fueler |
| --- |

### Meteorite Miners

Known Weaknesses: Shadow, Arcane, Law

The unfortunate mice caught up within the magic and mayhem of the fallen meteor around Fort Rox. Rough by day, terrifying by night!

A list of Meteorite Miners mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups, based on how late the Hunter hunts through the Night:

| Misc.<br>Weremice<br>Cosmic Critter<br>Special; and<br>Dawn Destroyer |
| --- |

### The Marching Flame

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Tactical, Hydro

All that lies in the path of The Marching Flame is destroyed. This force of mice has marched the desert for years conquering land and destroying settlements.

A list of The Marching Flame mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the type of fighting unit they belong to:

| Archer<br>Artillery<br>Cavalry<br>Mage | Scout<br>Warrior<br>Support; and<br>Command |
| --- | --- |

### Muridae Market Mice

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Tactical, Law

In wake of the Marching Flame's attack, these mice have taken claim on the Muridae Market. Rebuilding damaged shops has proven quite difficult due to these mice continuously stealing building materials as soon as they are delivered.

A list of the Muridae Market mice can be found here.

### Living Garden Mice

Known Weaknesses: Hydro

The armies of the Living Garden have really taken advantage of their environment, putting the local flora to use in crafting weapons and armour. But why are they gathering in such numbers?

A list of Living Garden mice can be found here.

### Lost City Mice

Known Weaknesses: Arcane

These mice were subjected to a terrible curse that has affected them all equally and terribly. However, nobody knows where the curse came from or who exactly was responsible and recriminations abound.

A list of Lost City mice can be found here.

### Sand Dunes Mice

Known Weaknesses: Shadow

Only tough and hardy mice can survive the dunes, but even they are wary and cautious around the ravenous Grubling Mice. A tenuous ecosystem flourishes in the dunes, where predators and prey both seek out food while avoiding dangerous stampedes.

A list of Sand Dunes mice can be found here.

### Queso Canyoneers

Known Weaknesses: Shadow, Arcane, Draconic, Law

Swimming in a sea of molten Queso, this vast canyon of smooth, buttery, liquid cheese has attracted a variety of spice loving mice looking for that perfect blend of Queso Cheese. Recently, dragon-like mice have joined these mice in their quest for queso.

A list of Queso Canyoneers mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the different stages and cheese used in each location:

| River Riders<br>Spice Mice<br>Quarry Quarries | Cork Collector<br>Pressure Builder; and<br>Geyser Hunter |
| --- | --- |

### Deep Sea Dwellers

Known Weaknesses: Hydro

Deep beneath the surface of the Rodentia Ocean lie the Deep Sea Dwellers. Centered around the Sunken City, there is an entire civilization of mice, isolated from the outside world, waiting to be discovered!

A list of Deep Sea Dwellers mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on how deep they are likely to be found in relation to Sunken City, and what loot they are likely to drop:

| Sunken City Citizens<br>Finned Fiend<br>Coral Corral<br>Barnacled Bunch | Scale Society<br>Treasure Troop; and<br>Predator Pack<br>*nocontent |
| --- | --- |

### Fungal Fiends

Known Weaknesses: Forgotten, Hydro

Crawling forth from the deep, dark and dank caves and caverns below are a few unique breeds of mice descending from a long line of rocks, crystals and fungus. Strange, marvelous and powerful! Creep carefully when crawling through these caverns!

A list of Fungal Fiends can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on how deep they are in the Fungal Cavern:

| Fungal Fodder<br>Gruyere Grazer<br>Mineral Muncher<br>Gemstone Gorger; and<br>Diamond Devourer |
| --- |

### Citizens of Zokor

Known Weaknesses: Arcane, Forgotten

Antiquated mice from an antiquated era. Locked away behind the lost Labyrinth, these mice have continued their existence protecting their city. If the Labyrinth doesn't get you, the mice will!

A list of the Citizens of Zokor can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the Labyrinth hallways and Zokor districts they reside in:

| Hallway Wanderer<br>Fungal Farmer<br>Lost Scholar<br>Fealty Sworn Soldier | Tech Engineer<br>Treasure Miser; and<br>Hidden Remnant |
| --- | --- |

### Moussu Picchu Inhabitants

Known Weaknesses: Arcane, Draconic, Shadow

Hidden away for years by the mountain ranges south of the Hollow Heights, these mice threaten to unleash a perfect storm of mischief should they ever advance towards Gnawnia.

A list of the Moussu Picchu Inhabitants mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on weather intensity of Moussu Picchu and cheese used:

| Fungal Feeder<br>Potion Brewer<br>Wind Wanderer<br>Rain Roamer; and<br>Storm Dragon |
| --- |

### Floating Islanders

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane, Forgotten, Hydro, Draconic, Law

High above the tallest mountain peaks, you'll find these light-hearted islanders basking in the sun. They lead a thrilling life of cloud chasing, island hopping, and high-altitude treasure hunting.

A list of Floating Islanders mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the islands they reside in and power types:

| Launch Pad<br>Cloud Commoner<br>Physical Pummeler<br>Shadow Overcaster | Tactical Dog Fighter<br>Atmospheric Arcane<br>Floating Forgotten<br>Hovering Hydro | Dashing Dragon<br>Lofty Lawbreaker<br>Sky Pirate<br>Sky Warden | Sky Paragon<br>Palace Protectors<br>The Richest; and<br>Empyrean Guard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

### Foreword Farmers

Known Weaknessess: Tactical

Some may call these mice the "Salt of the Earth" but a "Thorn in Your Side" would be more accurate. These pesky critters enjoy nothing more than digging in the dirt, nibbling on valuable crops, and preventing hard-working hunters from reaping the rewards of this farm's enchanted soil! Any standard cheese will lure them away from their crop-crunching but it'll take a strong Tactical trap to clear the farm of these persistent pests.

A list of Foreword Farmers can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the number of plants planted:

| Seed Stowers; and<br>Petulant Pests |
| --- |

### Prologue Pond Prowlers

Known Weakness: Hydro

This is not your typical fishing trip! These fresh water aquatic antagonists have a unique appetite for various types of clever but peculiar cheeses crafted from the items found in their pond. Make sure to load your boat with a hefty Hydro trap if you plan to venture out onto this precarious pond!

A list of Prologue Pond Prowlers can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the cheese used:

| Grub Gatherers<br>Shallow Swimmers; and<br>Deep Divers |
| --- |

### Storytellers

Known Weaknessess: Forgotten

This collection of creative characters is composed of the greatest authors ever to walk on four legs in addition to many of their most famous and infamous storybook characters. At the helm of this malicious magnum opus is the Mythweaver himself who is using these authors and their characters to rewrite the history of Gnawnia! Arm yourself with an assortment of Draft Derby cheese, a powerful Forgotten trap, and a great deal of ingenuity before facing off against these verbose villains!

A list of Storytellers can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the cheese used and the number of words written:

| Folklore Authors<br>Folklore Characters; and<br>Folklore Masterminds |
| --- |

### Beanstalkers

Known Weaknessess: Physical

From the bottom of the beanstalk all the way up to the Castle in the Clouds above, you'll find a vast assortment of challenging but valuable rodents. Arm yourself with an impressive Physical trap before climbing this stalk because whether you're facing guards in the Dungeon, socialites in the Ballroom, or nobles in the Great Hall, you've got a challenge ahead of you! Most of all, beware the wrath of the Giants because they don't take kindly to unwanted strangers waking them from their slumber!

A list of Beanstalkers can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the vine planted:

| Budding Baddies<br>Dungeon Dwellers<br>Ballroom Blitzers; and<br>Ruthless Royals |
| --- |

### Sorcery Apprentices

Known Weaknessess: Arcane, Shadow

The Mythweaver has been training a new generation of magical mice in the ways of Arcane and Shadow sorcery at this enchanted institution.

A list of Sorcery Apprentices can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the course taken:

| Monitor of the Halls<br>Arcane Academics<br>Master Sorcerers; and<br>Shadow Scholars |
| --- |

### Dragons of the Depths

Known Weaknessess: Draconic

Buried beneath the surface of Gnawnia lies a vast realm of ancient caverns inhabited by serpentine monsters that have remained hidden for untold centuries. These terrifying creatures have surfaced only occasionally in the past, taking control of whatever region they emerged from. But now that their underground lair has been exposed, these elemental enemies are eager to expand their horizons, take flight, and dominate the world above.

A list of Dragons of the Depths can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups, based on the cavern type the mice reside in:

| Fire Dragons<br>Ice Dragons<br>Poison Dragons; and<br>Elemental Dragons |
| --- |

### Afterword Anti-Arborists

Known Weaknessess: Tactical

This invasive species of arboreal mice are spreading a wretched blight throughout the Afterword Acres in an attempt to poison and destroy the Infinitree.

A list of Afterword Anti-Arborists can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups:

| Foliage Fomenters<br>Brushwood Bruisers<br>Deciduous Destroyers<br>Coniferous Corrupters; and<br>Blight Bringers |
| --- |

### Epilogue Ecosystem

Known Weaknessess: Hydro

These mischevious, marine mice are a menace to the ecosystem and they seem intent on guarding the glorious and gargantuan falls at the end of the rapids.

A list of Epilogue Ecosystem mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups:

| Coastal Crawlers<br>Slow Sea Shrubs<br>Agile Algae Eaters<br>Speedy Shellfish; and<br>Torrential Tyrants |
| --- |

### Conclusion Cliffhangers

Known Weaknessess: Law

These infamous characters from throughout Gnawnian literature, spanning multiple works and genres, are the Mythweaver's final weapon against the MouseHunters. Conclude the Mythweaver's story by clashing with this colourful cast of characters and correcting their content conclusively.

A list of Conclusion Cliffhangers mice can be found here. These mice are further divided into sub-groups:

| Prose Proprietors<br>Adventurous Adversaries<br>Comedic Caricatures<br>Romantic Rivals<br>Suspenseful Scoundrels<br>Tragic Troublemakers<br>Fantasy Fanatics<br>Lore Weavers |
| --- |

### Rift Walkers

Known Weaknesses: Rift

Located in another dimension, the Gnawnia Rift Walkers are the supreme archetypes of the Gnawnian mice. Surrounded by swirls of Rift energy, they possess power beyond belief. Even the greatest of mouse-hunting technology poses little threat to these magical, mysterious mice. To all MouseHunters seeking to challenge these mice: Steel yourselves, bring your courage, and do not let fear overcome you.

A list of Rift Walkers mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups, based on the locations the mice reside in:

| Gnawnia Rift<br>Burroughs Rift; and<br>Whisker Woods Rift |
| --- |

### Rift Stalkers

Known Weaknesses: Rift

The Rift Stalkers are terrifying predators from beyond the Rift, exemplars of their kind. Far more powerful than the previously-encountered Rift Walkers. The only things that can harm them are specially-crafted Rift traps. Make sure you're properly equipped before taking on these deadly mice!

A list of Rift Stalkers mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups, based on the locations the mice reside in:

| Furoma Rift<br>Bristle Woods Rift; and<br>Valour Rift |
| --- |

### The Polluted

Known Weaknesses: Hydro

Sticky, Gross, Smelly and Strange. These mice have been exposed to the evils of the Laboratory for far too long and have now developed some interesting side effects! Whether it be from the pollution or the repeated strange experiments they were put through, you wont believe them until you see them!

A list of The Polluted mice can be found here.

### Event Mice

Known Weaknesses: Physical, Shadow, Tactical, Arcane, Forgotten, Hydro, Draconic, Law, Rift

These mice are released occasionally during various parts of the year. Each is fairly unique, often requiring a specific hunting strategy.

A list of Event Mice can be found here. The mice in this group are further divided into sub-groups:

| Lunar New Year<br>Birthday<br>Spring Egg Hunt<br>Halloween | Great Winter Hunt<br>New Year<br>Prize<br>Ronza's Stowaways |

Hunters can encounter the Mousevina von Vermin in the Mousoleum only.

Hunters must capture the Mousevina von Vermin in the Mousoleum location in order to obtain the Shredded Furoma Map Piece.

The Shredded Furoma Map Piece allows Hunters to access the Training Grounds location.

Hunters can take the Shredded Furoma Map Piece to the Bazaar Cartographer to repair it and obtain the Stitched Furoma Map Piece which allows Hunters to access the Dojo, Meditation Room, and Pinnacle Chamber locations.

## Preferred Cheese

Mystic King mice have no specific preference for any kind of cheese.

## Hunting Strategy

The weaknesses of the Mystic King mouse differ slightly from most others in the Wizard's Pieces group. Tactical weapons are very effective against it, while all others are ineffective. It is only available to attract after a Mystic Queen mouse has been caught.

Upon capturing a Mystic King mouse, the hunter is automatically transported back to the Seasonal Garden unless they are using either Checkmate Cheese or a Stalemate Charm. By using either Checkmate Cheese or a Stalemate Charm, a hunter is able to remain in Zugzwang's Tower and attempt to capture additional mice, including the Chess Master.

Upon capturing a Mystic King mouse with either Checkmate Cheese or a Stalemate Charm armed, the mouse population changes. If Checkmate Cheese is armed, the available mice will be the Chess Master, Mystic Rook and whichever Technic mice have been unlocked. If Standard Cheese is armed, the available mice will be the Mystic Pawn and whichever Technic mice have been unlocked.

## Event Participation

### Spring Egg Hunt

- The Mystic King Mouse drops the Mystic King Egg during the annual Spring Egg Hunt.

| After losing his tenure at the School of Sorcery, the relentless and resourceful Mythweaver came to realize that fantasy alone would not be enough to finally defeat the pesky humans and their persistent MouseHunters. He realized that he would need something much bigger and more terrifying this time. He needed something that struck to the very core of human fear, that burrowed deep into the psyche of MouseHunters and awakened some primal terror that has remained dormant since the time of their most ancient ancestors. He needed something so great and terrible that it would instantly remind the humans of their lowly place in the hierarchy of species.<br>After much searching, he eventually discovered a book much older and more primitive than the folktales he had been rewriting thus far. This book described a very different world with very different masters from a time long before the age of humans. A time that was ruled by fear and ferociousness, where only the mightiest and most ruthless survived and thrived; a time when mercy, compassion, and civilization were concepts yet to be discovered. T'was the time of dragons!<br>The Mythweaver studied the Tale of the First Dragons extensively and learned a most shocking and fortuitous discovery: the age of dragons had not ended, it was merely awaiting the beginning of its next chapter! And so, with quill in hand, inhibitions unfettered, and delusions of grandeur abound, he set upon that most villainous deed of penning the next chapter himself.<br>He followed the directions spelled out in the book and it led him deep below the Folklore Forest to a place that time forgot: the Draconic Depths. Deep within these coarse, cacophonous caverns, the Mythweaver discovered the hidden home and true origin of all the dragons in Gnawnia. Every great dragon that he had studied from the world above could trace its origins back to these dark and dangerous depths. From the furious flames of Kalor'ignis to the frigid ferocity of Icewing and all the way back to the great Dragon mouse itself. All of these legendary beasts once called these depths their home.<br>Here the Mythweaver had everything he needed to amass the greatest and most terrible army of ancient monsters with which to lay waste to the human world above. So he used every ounce of his fabled magic to transform himself into the mightiest dragon of them all and named himself their Emperor. Now he intends to lead this legendary legion up to the surface and dispose of the human Kingdom of Gnawnia once and for all. That is, unless the strongest and bravest MouseHunters can face their fears and descend into these dreadful depths to put a stop to this heinous plan before it takes flight! |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 1209 |  |  |

Only Draconic power types are effective against Mythical Dragon Emperor.
All other types are ineffective.

| Location & Attraction Info |  |  |  |

| Many a cautionary tale has been written about the dangers of hubris but few are as poignant or consequential as the one being penned by the Mythweaver.<br>This once meek and meager mouse began its story as a simple Bookborn willed into existence by the maniacal Zurreal the Eternal. There was something unique about this particular manifestation however and it caused Zurreal to take special notice. This Bookborn exhibited more intelligence, intuition, and understanding than the rest of its kind and so Zurreal decided to share small fragments of his immense knowledge with this curious creature. As the Bookborn consumed more knowledge, its abilities began to grow and so too did its usefulness. Zurreal recognized an opportunity to mold and shape this exceptional creation into a powerful assistant capable of expediting his plans to conquer humans and mice alike.<br>Unbeknownst to Zurreal, this creature was consuming knowledge at an unimaginable rate and before long, its intelligence and understanding had begun to surpass even its master's. This nameless creation eventually sought to have an identity of its own and, having developed a particular fascination with the countless volumes of folklore contained in the Crystal Library, began calling itself the Mythweaver. The Mythweaver began to recognize that he was merely a servant to an insane and tyrannical leader, a mere cog in a broken machine. And with that profound realization, this ethereal creature transformed into a unique and extraordinarily powerful mouse! On that day, the Mythweaver vowed to turn against his creator and become a true leader of mice; dedicated not only to their survival but to their supremacy in the land of Gnawnia!<br>So the Mythweaver scoured every inch of the great library in search of a means by which he could conquer the kingdom on behalf of his kind and one day he found what he had been searching for. Hidden inside a forgotten book on a forgotten shelf, the Mythweaver discovered a single page that Zurreal had missed all these years. This enchanted page was written by Zugzwang himself and on it he learned of a secret place of unprecedented power: the Folklore Forest!<br>He learned that deep in the Folklore Forest there exists a magical Book of Lore which contains the entire history of Gnawnia scribbled throughout its pages. What is special about this book however, is that if the words on these pages are changed then so too will history itself be changed. And thus began the Mythweaver's quest to rewrite history by writing the mice as the glorious champions and the humans as the vanquished foes! |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 1113 |  |  |

## Cheese Preference

Mythweaver is only attracted to Final Draft Derby Cheese.

## Hunting Strategy

Mythweaver is only available when the stage is writing and the Hunter has written at least 4,000 words in the current writing session.

Forgotten power type is very effective against Mythweaver.
All other types are ineffective.

## Loot

Mythweaver can drop:

- Ancient Relic
- Condensed Creativity
- Divine Orb
- Gnawbel Prize for Literature
- Enchanted Page

With Leather Bound Cover, the following loot is added to the pool:

- Cleverness Clam
- Crop Coin
- Inspiration Ink
- Mythical Mulch
- Pond Penny
- Papyrus Seed
- Parable Papyrus

With Silver Quill and Golden Quill, the following loot is added to the pool:

- Rainbow Nib

Obstinate Oboist Mouse is a breed of mouse found on the Ballroom Floor in Bountiful Beanstalk.

| Obstinate Oboist Mouse |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: Beanstalkers (Ballroom Blitzers) |  |  |  |
| Mouse Statistics |  |  |  |
| Points: | 80,000 | Gold: | 12,000 |
| Location & Attraction Info |  |  |  |
| Required Power Types: | Physical | Other Requirements: | Ballroom Floor |
| Cheese: | Beanster Cheese | Charm: | None |
| Locations: | Bountiful Beanstalk | Loot: | Golden Harp StringRoyal Ruby Bean |
| Links |  |  |  |
| Larry's Loot Lexicon: | MouseHunt Info Page | Image: | Image Link |
| It is not uncommon for an extremely passionate and tirelessly devoted artist to be viewed as stubborn. However, there are those who take that distinction to a whole new level. This very talented but completely unreasonable Oboist is one such musician who, much to the chagrin of the rest of the orchestra, has dedicated their life in pursuit of a single, very strange, and rather irritating goal: to master the "infinite note"! No one really knows how long the Obstinate Oboist has been siting there playing this one note but it feels like an eternity and no amount of desperate pleading seems capable of deterring them from this utterly asinine endeavour. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 1144 |  |  |

## Cheese Preference

Obstinate Oboist Mouse is only attracted to Beanster Cheese.

## Hunting Strategy

The Obstinate Oboist Mouse can only be attracted after planting a Medium Vine to the Ballroom Floor.

Physical power type is effective against Obstinate Oboist Mouse.
All other types are ineffective.

## Loot

Obstinate Oboist Mouse can drop:

- Golden Harp String
- Royal Ruby Bean

Red Coat Bear mice have been found to be especially attracted to String Cheese, to the point that any other kind of cheese will simply not suffice.

The Red Coat Bear Mouse is weak to Rift Traps. It can only be attracted by String Cheese.

## Event Participation

### Spring Egg Hunt

- The Red Coat Bear Mouse drops the Enlarged Rift Egg and the Rift Mist Egg during the annual Spring Egg Hunt.

# 🐭 Mouse: Relic Hunter Mouse

> **Type**: Mouse | **Category**: Mice | **Source**: [Relic Hunter Mouse](https://mhwiki.hitgrab.com/wiki/index.php/Relic_Hunter_Mouse)

| Relic Hunter Mouse |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: Indigenous Mice (Rare Rodent) |  |  |  |
| Mouse Statistics |  |  |  |
| Points: | 650 | Gold: | 935 |
| Location & Attraction Info |  |  |  |
| Required Power Types: | All Power Types except Parental | Other Requirements: | None |
| Cheese: | None | Charm: | None |
| Locations: | Randomly changes every 24 hours.See Locations section below. | Loot: | Ancient Relic |
| Links |  |  |  |
| Larry's Loot Lexicon: | MouseHunt Info Page | Image: | Image Link |
| For many years, the Relic Hunter Mouse scoured the Kingdom of Gnawnia in search of precious Ancient Relics and would steal them from unsuspecting hunters wherever she went. At long last, her search has finally completed and she has collected so many Ancient Relics that she can now undertake her ultimate goal of using them to decipher the true origin of mice in Gnawnia and why they came here; an ancient mystery that has been lost to the ages. Now she travels all around the Kingdom, studying the wonders of each place she visits, and using the Ancient Relics as the key to unlocking the secrets of murine prehistory.<br>The Relic Hunter Mouse is restless and obsessive, traveling to a new location every day, as she tries to solve her great mystery. Hunters who are looking to obtain Ancient Relics for their own purposes can attempt to decipher the clues she leaves behind to locate this elusive mouse. Once she's been located, simply hunt in that location and she'll occasionally pass by your trap. She is too preoccupied to bother with your cheese or charm but if you manage to catch her, you'll be able to loot some of her precious Ancient Relics! |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 401 |  |  |

## Attracting the Relic Hunter Mouse

Each hunt in the current location of the Relic Hunter Mouse, both through sounding the Hunter's Horn and the hourly trap check, has the potential to attract the Relic Hunter Mouse in addition to any mice that may be attracted to the Hunter's Cheese.
Encountering a Relic Hunter Mouse will not affect progress in any area when encountered.

The attraction of the Relic Hunter Mouse is not affected by any Cheese or Charms.

### Bonus Hunt

A successful catch of the Relic Hunter Mouse will occur as a bonus hunt that does not consume either Cheese or Charms.
The outcome of the main hunt, whether it is a successful catch, failure to catch or failure to attract, has no impact on the outcome of the Relic Hunter Mouse's bonus hunt.

## Locations

Every 24 hours, the Relic Hunter Mouse randomly moves to one of the following locations.
There is a chance for the Relic Hunter Mouse to move to the current location it was at, effectively staying at the same location for more than 24 hours.
Viewing the Treasure Map popup under the Invites and Scroll Cases tab offers a hint to the Relic Hunter's current location.

Note: The Relic Hunter Mouse appears in the Living Garden and Twisted Garden at the same time.

| Once young and lively, this minotaur loved racing through the hallways of the Labyrinth, chasing down hunters and mice alike, howling and bellowing with delight as they scurried at the mere sound of his hooves on the cobbled floors. But now, it seems he has run his last lap of the maze, and has settled down into cozy end-life routines. Donning his fuzzy slippers in his favourite easy chair (which is a giant sack of gold), this retired beast has had his pension paid out in full and has relocated to his secret inner chamber to enjoy his retirement in peace and quiet.<br>The same shenanigans that used to bring him joy now only cause him grief, and he can be seen shaking his fist from atop his tower at the other mice hustling and bustling in the city. All that noise, all that racket! What a grumpy old grump this once playful beast has become...<br>But even in his twilight and seemingly endless misery, he still manages to let a small grin spread across his lips whenever he causes a mouse to jump in fear at the sound of his snort or the clipping of his hooves.<br>No one has broken into his private chambers and lived to tell the tale. |  | Mouse ID#: 782 |  |  |

## Preferred Cheese

The Retired Minotaur Mouse prefers Glowing Gruyere, but can be attracted with Standard Cheeses.

## Hunting Strategy

Forgotten weapons are very effective against the Retired Minotaur Mouse. Arcane weapons are of normal effectiveness.

The Retired Minotaur Mouse can only be found in the Lair of the Minotaur. While it can be encountered at any time within the Lair of the Minotaur after the Hunter has caught any one mouse, it is more easily attracted and caught as its state (as indicated in the HUD) moves closer to Reckless. Hunters may only catch one Retired Minotaur Mouse per visit to the Lair of the Minotaur.

Hunters are returned to the beginning of the Labyrinth upon catching a Retired Minotaur Mouse.

## Loot

The Retired Minotaur Mouse will drop a variety of loot from the following list:

- Charms

- Crafting Items

- Orbs

- Miscellaneous Items

Arming any of the various Anchor Charms will prevent a Hunter from being washed out when capturing a Riptide Mouse.

He's usually on a westerly wagon to the Sandtail Desert by now, but the Festive Comet unfortunately landed right on top of his wagon before he boarded. Now, he's a bit stranded and, as you can imagine, a bit cold!<br>This mouse has meticulously planned his retirement around being just the right amount of warm all year; never too hot, and never, ever too cold. So much thought has gone into this lifestyle decision that he has changed his whole wardrobe to revolve around only wearing his favourite summer apparel: Shorts!<br>Stubborn as ever, he has put his engineering know-how (and most of his retirement savings) towards developing quite the sophisticated network of portable heaters to heat things up a bit! Nothing will get in this mouse's way when it comes to enjoying his retirement!<br>He is not letting a little snow ruin his plans for having his fun in the sun this winter, but the sudden rapid heating near the Festive Comet is threatening to thaw the Winter Hunt cheer too early this year and he must be stopped! |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 1011 |  |  |

| With the methodical moves of a ticking clock, the Technic King pushes his armies into battle, calculating their attacks using cold, hard logic. If this King needs to lose a few pawns to gain the victory, so be it. He's also not afraid to use a little firepower, as evidenced by the secret weapon hiding under his crown. ## Preferred Cheese

Technic King mice have no specific preference for any kind of cheese.

## Hunting Strategy

The weaknesses of the Technic King Mouse differ slightly from most others in the Wizard's Pieces group. Tactical weapons are very effective against it, while all the others are less effective. It is only available to attract after a Technic Queen mouse has been caught.

Upon capturing a Technic King mouse, the hunter is automatically transported back to the Seasonal Garden unless they are using either Checkmate Cheese or a Stalemate Charm. By using either Checkmate Cheese or a Stalemate Charm a hunter is able to remain in Zugzwang's Tower and attempt to capture additional mice, including the Chess Master.

Upon capturing a Technic King mouse with either Checkmate Cheese or a Stalemate Charm armed, the mouse population changes. If Checkmate Cheese is armed, the available mice will be the Chess Master, Technic Rook and whichever Mystic mice have been unlocked. If Standard Cheese is armed, the available mice will be the Technic Pawn and whichever Mystic mice have been unlocked.

## Event Participation

### Spring Egg Hunt

- The Technic King Mouse drops the Technic King Egg during the annual Spring Egg Hunt.

## Preferred Cheese

Tentacle mice are attracted to Magical Rancid Radioactive Blue at every spill level and to Rancid Radioactive Blue when spill level is for Count/Countess and above.

Hydro type traps such as Oasis Water Node Trap or Phantasmic Oasis Trap are effective against the Tentacle Mouse.

## Event Participation

- The Tentacle Mouse drops the Toxic Spill Egg during the annual Spring Egg Hunt.

| Terrified of heights, this battle-hardened adventurer is determined to conquer his fear by climbing the tower to the top! It doesn't help that the design of the tower is an endless upwards spiral. Looking up is just as terrifying as looking down! |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 1008 |  |  |

## Floor Type Info

- The Terrified Adventurer Mouse can be found on All Floors except Eclipse.
Capturing the Terrified Adventurer Mouse advances the Hunter up the Valour Rift tower 2X steps, where X is the Hunter's Speed level.
Capturing the Terrified Adventurer Mouse with Champion's Fire enabled advances the Hunter up the tower by 2X+2 steps.
The String Stepping augmentation doubles the progress made when capturing the Terrified Adventurer Mouse:
Capturing the Terrified Adventurer Mouse with String Stepping but not Champion's Fire enabled advances the Hunter up the tower by 4X steps.
Capturing the Terrified Adventurer Mouse with both String Stepping and Champion's Fire enabled advances the Hunter up the tower by 4X+4 steps.
- The Terrified Adventurer Mouse has a Minimum Floor of 1.

## Loot

- Champion's Fire
- Simple Orb
- Tattered Celestial Skin Pattern
- The Gilded Steps – Can only be obtained at Floor 100+ of the Valour Rift tower.
- Tower Sigil

# 🐭 Mouse: Ultimate Mythweaver

> **Type**: Mouse | **Category**: Mice | **Source**: [Ultimate Mythweaver](https://mhwiki.hitgrab.com/wiki/index.php/Ultimate_Mythweaver)

Ultimate Mythweaver is a breed of mouse found on the in Conclusion Cliffs.

| Ultimate Mythweaver |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse Group: Conclusion Cliffhangers (Lore Weavers) |  |  |  |
| Mouse Statistics |  |  |  |
| Points: | 1,250,000 | Gold: | 225,000 |
| Location & Attraction Info |  |  |  |
| Required Power Types: | Law | Other Requirements: |  |
| Cheese: | Plotting PaneerStoried SagaDeus Ex Maconnais | Charm: | None |
| Locations: | Conclusion Cliffs | Loot: |  |
| Links |  |  |  |
| Larry's Loot Lexicon: | MouseHunt Info Page | Image: | Image Link |
| The long and winding road through the Folklore Forest has been wrought with perils both for the MouseHunters and the Mythweaver alike. But alas, all stories must eventually end and this one finds its climax here at the great precipice known as the Conclusion Cliffs.<br>Since his humble beginnings as a lowly Bookborn under the tutelage of Zurreal the Eternal, this aspirational adversary has sought to overthrow the King of Gnawnia and bring about the end of human supremacy. He used the transformative magic of the Folklore Forest to write himself multiple new identities, each with the goal of being the one that would finally defeat the MouseHunters and lead the mice to victory. First he attempted to rewrite history at the Table of Contents and then tried to write himself into all of Gnawnia's great folktales but he was stopped at every turn by the fearless, relentless hunters who pursued him.<br>Now he has finally come to the end of his road at the top of the towering Conclusion Cliffs where the MouseHunters of Gnawnia have backed him into a corner. In his last ditch attempt to fight back, he has split himself into multiple versions based on the five main literary genres. Each version has assembled its own army of mice adapted from the most famous and infamous literary characters of their respective genres. This, the truest and most ultimate form of the Mythweaver, remains protected by the unimaginable power of the greatest genre of all: Fantasy!<br>However, if the hunters can demonstrate their writing prowess by earning Notoriety in all of the main genres then they will prove their ability to write a Fantasy tale so great that the Mythweaver will be unable to resist the challenge. Only then will the MouseHunters finally be able to close the book on this sinister storyteller for good and seal him in a just conclusion for eternity.<br>One loose end that the King's best scholars have been unable to decipher all this time is: how exactly did a meek and meager Bookborn amass profound, devastating, otherworldly power to the extent that it was capable of raising a massive, sprawling army and ravaging an entire region? There is some piece of this puzzle that has yet to be found. Perhaps some force, far greater and more mysterious still, that has played a pivotal role in this malevolent mouse's meteoric rise to power. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 1292 |  |  |

## Cheese Preference

Ultimate Mythweaver is attracted to Plotting Paneer or Storied Saga or Deus Ex Maconnais.

## Hunting Strategy

The Ultimate Mythweaver can only be attracted while writing a postscript to a story.

Only Law power types are effective against Ultimate Mythweaver.
All other types are ineffective.

# 🐭 Mouse: Unknown Mouse

> **Type**: Mouse | **Category**: Mice | **Source**: [Unknown Mouse](https://mhwiki.hitgrab.com/wiki/index.php/Unknown_Mouse)

An Unknown Mouse is a mouse that has yet to be caught by a hunter. These mice are usually either new or very rare. Unknown mice are displayed with a placeholder image of a question mark, which is later replaced by a silhouette of the mouse after it has been caught for the first time. Despite being unknown, the MouseHunt Info Page will still provides the power and power type of the mouse. It will also include either a description of the mouse or a note saying that the hunter has not yet discovered a location where the mouse resides.

| Convecting the heat from Hot Queso straight into the air around it, this mouse heats the ground below it, acting as a thermal conductor to increase the pressure of the geyser. |  |  |  |
|  | Mouse ID#: 981 |  |  |

## Cheese and Charm Preference

### Cheese

The Vaporior Mouse is only attracted to Hot Queso or Flamin' Queso.

### Charm

No Charms are required to attract the Vaporior Mouse.

## Hunting Strategy

Catching a Vaporior Mouse while building pressure in Queso Geyser increases the amount of pressure by 40 kPa.

Only Draconic traps are effective against the Vaporior Mouse, all other power types are ineffective. The Vaporior Mouse can only be encountered while building pressure in Queso Geyser, after a cork has been constructed.

Dragonbane Charm, Super Dragonbane Charm, Extreme Dragonbane Charm, and Ultimate Dragonbane Charm provide a power bonus against the Vaporior Mouse.

The ⚡Thunderlord⚡ has been found to be especially attracted to Dragonvine Cheese cheese, to the point that any other kind of cheese will simply not suffice.

## Power Type Weaknesses

| VeryEffective | Effective | Less Effective |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Draconic | None | None |

## Hunting Strategy

Only Draconic type traps are effective against the ⚡Thunderlord⚡, all other power types are ineffective.

Dragonbane Charms, Super Dragonbane Charms and Extreme Dragonbane Charms provide a power bonus against the ⚡Thunderlord⚡.

The ⚡Thunderlord⚡ is only available when both wind and rain intensities are at least between 35%-79% in Moussu Picchu.
